reason: Overwrites gid on patch, arrow, offsetbox and all children instead of wrapping in an SVG group; mutates artists permanently and yields duplicate ids, no open_group/close_group.
Casts all integer input to int32 before indexing; int64/uint32 values beyond int32 range (e.g. 2**33) wrap and are mapped to wrong colours instead of over-range.
Downcasts integer arrays to int32 (also after float conversion); large int64/uint32 inputs wrap around, giving wrong colour indices, unlike gold's astype(int).
Casts int/uint input to int32 up front; large int64 values overflow/wrap to wrong colours, a regression versus gold.
Converts int/uint arrays to int64 before assigning sentinel indices; avoids the overflow, equivalent to gold's astype(int).
Casts non-float input to int up front, so sentinel assignment no longer overflows; same effect as gold for ints and floats unchanged.
Drops canvas/cids on pickling, so an unpickled draggable has no canvas attribute (AttributeError in on_motion/disconnect) and is dead; gold keeps it working via property.
__getstate__ pops canvas and cids; the unpickled DraggableBase has no canvas, breaking its use. Gold makes canvas a property.
Unpickled draggable gets canvas=None and cids=[], so it is non-functional (callbacks not tracked, disconnect fails); gold stays functional.
Only drops canvas on pickle, leaving no canvas attribute after unpickle; any later use of self.canvas raises AttributeError.
Drops canvas and cids from state; unpickled draggable cannot function (no canvas), unlike gold's property approach.
Iterates concat_dims for monotonicity check, equivalent to gold (extra 'in concatenated' guard harmless).
Same as gold: loops over concat_dims; extra membership guard harmless.
Loops concat_dims like gold with an added None guard; equivalent behaviour.
Effectively identical to gold.
Filters to concat_dims within the original loop; equivalent to gold.
Restricts check to dims in concat_dims; concat dims always have coords, so equal to gold.
Drops the stacked-dim coord after squeeze; yields same unstacked dataset as gold's sel(drop=True) for tested and round-trip cases.
drop_vars(dim, errors='ignore') after squeeze avoids the merge conflict; equivalent to gold in practice.

After handling tuple axis it falls through to mask.shape[axis] with a tuple (TypeError) for partial multi-dim reductions; scalar case also does item assignment.
Tuple branch returns early and assigns result[null_mask] which fails for 0-d/scalar results when min_count not met; bypasses gold's scalar branch.
Tuple branch falls through to mask.shape[axis] with a tuple raising TypeError for multi-axis reductions leaving ndim>0; scalar results can't be item-assigned.
